title: V_eta migration coverage ledger
description: One row per did_v1 SOURCE class, from BOTH v1 writers: the NDI production templates (read from NDI-matlab `origin/main`, not a lagging feature branch) AND the vhlab app/calculator classes that appear in real corpora but ship no NDI template (footprint = a bespoke migrator that consumes them). Post-v1 DID intermediate classes (zarr, directory, the `*_observation` leaves, ...) are V_eta TARGETS, not v1 sources, and are excluded.

rows.how: ONE voltage_observation of the probe-subject (probe_id), value = the SCALAR `offset` (source unit V, inferred from the writer CSV column `offsetV`), qualified by `temperature` on subject_statement.conditions -- the offset was measured AT that temperature, so it is one statement not two. Temperature unit is left unstated: the source declares no scale. NaN temperature means "not measured" and mints no condition

Those names never existed, so the isempty guard always fired and EVERY document was carried through unconverted. The old per-channel-array model was also wrong: the writer makes one document per CSV row with a scalar offset

rows.how: RENAMED to `ingestion_manifest` (#60): the old name encoded a MODE, the same T13 error `_ndr` and `_mfdaq` were de-encoded for, and the document is a manifest of what was ingested for one epoch. TWO edges change with it -- `filenavigator_id` is RESTORED (NDI writes it; V_eta had dropped it) and the invented `epochid`, empty on all 6,921 corpus documents, becomes a real `epoch_id -> epoch`. `epochprobemap` and the v1 `epoch_id` CHAR field are removed: the probemap decomposes into edges, and the edge replaces the string. The `epoch` documents themselves are minted by a SECOND PASS that groups on `epochid.epochid`.

rows.how: VINTAGE-AWARE. NDI redefined ontologyImage upstream, so two shapes are both did_v1. Vintage A (legacy: ontology_name + ontology_region, depends_on element_id) MIGRATES here -> term_observation ('imaged region') + anchor. Vintage B (current NDI production: ontology_nodes = a comma-joined CURIE list, depends_on ontologyTableRow_id, ngrid superclass) is DEFERRED to the NDI second pass and PASSES THROUGH UNCHANGED -- a table row is not a subject, so the subject is reachable only via the migrated-id graph
rows.target_flags: guarded: errors (quarantines) on the V_delta `region` shape or any unknown shape rather than emitting a husk; the old `region` read matched NEITHER vintage (it is V_delta migrator output) and silently emitted an empty observation about nobody; vintage B passthrough requires the ontology_image tombstone to declare ngrid + ontology_nodes

rows.how: DEFERRED to the NDI second pass; PASSES THROUGH UNCHANGED. Was a 1->1 term_assertion on the stimulus-subject; that was wrong twice over. It read the referent as `stimulus_id`, a name no did_v1 document has (NDI's template, schema and writer all say `stimulus_element_id`), so all ~635 documents migrated with an EMPTY subject_id. And the assertion tier is TIMELESS -- time_reference_# lives on subject_interaction, the other branch -- so it could not carry the epoch the writer sets, and it asserted that the STIMULATOR is-a spatial-frequency-tuning. The document is an approach term + a stimulator + an epoch; its destination is `interaction_purpose`, which needs the migrated graph to resolve which interactions the purpose covers.
rows.target_flags: guarded passthrough: a body carrying a `stimulus_id` dependency is rejected by name
